title: Efficient quantum Gibbs sampling of stabilizer codes using hybrid computation
authors: Ivan H C Shum and Angela Capel
abstract: We present hybrid Gibbs sampling algorithms for the stabilizer code Hamiltonians of the rotated surface code and the toric code with only local quantum algorithms, using quantum circuit depth to prepare the Gibbs state of the rotated surface code Hamiltonian, and quantum circuit depth to prepare the Gibbs state of the toric code Hamiltonian, being the side of the side of the square lattice. We further show that if we allow for non-local gates, the Gibbs state of the periodic 1D Ising model can be prepared in logarithmic depth and linearly many simultaneous measurements.

title: An active Lorentz gas: walking droplets in periodic media
authors: Aleksi Majaniemi, Esko Toivonen, Rahil N Valani, Rainer Klages and Esa Räsänen
abstract: The Lorentz gas is a paradigmatic model in dynamical systems theory for understanding the origin of nonequilibrium transport in terms of microscopic deterministic chaos. In the periodic setting, a point particle scatters elastically off disks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice. Here we replace the disks by smooth potentials and the particle by the widely studied walking droplet, which propels itself on a vertically vibrating fluid. In the low-memory limit, this droplet reduces to a particle with nonlinear active friction. We call this system an active Lorentz gas. Using extensive numerical simulations, we analyse how dissipation generated by the active deterministic dynamics alters the phase-space structure of the corresponding conservative Lorentz gas. We find that islands of stability collapse into attracting and repelling sets. To characterize these structures, we introduce an energy-variance filtering method that distinguishes localized periodic, quasi-ballistic periodic, and chaotic trajectories, enabling the construction of bifurcation diagrams in a non-conservative setting. We identify parameter regimes exhibiting strong bifurcation cascades, anomalous diffusion, and significant phase-space contraction. Our results establish the active Lorentz gas as a rich framework for studying transport in dissipative dynamical systems and provide a bridge between active matter and classical models of chaotic transport, with potential implications for hydrodynamic quantum analogs in periodic media.

title: Coupled propagation of acoustic topological states
authors: Ming-Zhu Li, Lei Shi, Zhe-Yu Ji, Zhaojiang Chen and Ya-Xi Shen
abstract: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupled propagation of two pseudospin states in an acoustic topological heterostructure. Within the framework of coupled-mode theory, the heterostructure is mapped onto a two-waveguide model, in which the two pseudospin topological states serve as guiding modes. The propagation constants of the individual topological states and the coupling strength between them are quantitatively extracted from the projected band structures of supercells. When the two topological states are decoupled, acoustic energy remains confined to the excited topological interface. When the two topological states are coupled, acoustic energy undergoes Bloch oscillation between two topological interfaces. Notably, the energy-transfer coefficient of the Bloch oscillation can be tuned by introducing interface detuning. Owing to the frequency dispersion of the coupling strength, the heterostructure can function as a wavelength-selective demultiplexer. This work establishes a generalized coupled-mode framework for the quantitative analysis and flexible manipulation of topological-state coupling, offering new insights into the design of topologically protected acoustic devices with controllable multichannel functionalities.

title: 2D quantum-path interference in high-harmonic generation driven by highly-bichromatic fields
authors: Xiaozhou Zou, Lucie Jurkovičová, Anne Weber, Cong Zhao, Martin Albrecht, Ondřej Finke, Alexandr Vendl, Annika Grenfell, Wojciech Szuba, Jaroslav Nejdl, Eric Constant, Margarita Khokhlova, Emilio Pisanty, Ondřej Hort and Amelle Zaïr
abstract: We experimentally observe a new type of quantum-path interference, in two-dimensions (2D-QPI), in high-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by an orthogonally-polarised highly-bichromatic field. This regime is characterised by a relatively strong orthogonal second-harmonic component beyond the weak perturbation limit, such that the electron dynamics are substantially modified. In this highly-bichromatic regime, we demonstrate that 2D-QPI is encoded in the measured harmonic intensity modulations with respect to the relative phase of the two-colour field. The modulations of the odd-order harmonics show a monomodal behaviour, whereas the even harmonics are modulated in a bimodal structure. Our calculations using the strong-field approximation and saddle-point method disentangle contributions from multiple quantum orbits in this HHG regime, revealing that the dipole response for both odd and even harmonics inherits the dynamic symmetry of the orthogonally-polarised driving field. This new type of 2D-QPI offers a novel route to HHG spectroscopy of attosecond electron dynamics by lifting up the dimensionality of the quantum paths involved in the interference.

title: Coherent receiver for continuous-variable quantum key distribution using a 3 × 3 beam splitter and single-ended photodetectors
authors: Pol Adillon, Samael Sarmiento, Jeison Tabares, Hugues de Riedmatten and Sebastian Etcheverry
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (QKD) relies on coherent detection. Conventional coherent receivers typically use an optical 90° hybrid and two balanced photodetectors providing robust phase-diversity detection. Here, we introduce and characterize a simplified receiver architecture based on a symmetric 3 × 3 beam splitter (BS) and three single-ended photodetectors for continuous-variable QKD. Results demonstrate that the 3 × 3 BS-based architecture provides similar performance to conventional ones while reducing optical-hardware complexity.

title: Magnon-mediated cooling by heating in a spin-selective quantum dot system
abstract: We demonstrate how nonequilibrium magnons can drive the cooling by heating effect in a spin-selective quantum dot system. The mechanism relies on magnon-assisted spin-flip transitions that transfer electrons between two ferromagnetic electrodes maintained at different temperatures, with the magnetic insulator acting as the high-temperature energy source. In the limit of fully spin-polarized antiparallel electrodes, the transport enters a tight-coupling regime in which each absorbed magnon is accompanied by the transfer of a single electron. This one-to-one correspondence directly links the cooling power to the heat supplied by the magnonic reservoir and enables the thermodynamic performance to approach its upper bound. We further show how finite spin polarization introduces parasitic spin channels that suppress cooling and reduce the operating range. An extended dual quantum dot configuration restores cooling by heating without net charge current and enhances the cooling power. Our results establish magnons as a distinct microscopic energy carrier for cooling by heating and provide a route toward its realization in solid-state spin-caloritronic systems.

title: Particle dynamics in constant synthetic non-abelian fields: I. the classical treatment
authors: Subramanya Bhat K N, Amita Das, Bhooshan Paradkar and V Ravishankar
abstract: Yang–Mills (YM) theory has evolved beyond its origins in the strong interaction to become an effective framework for condensed matter, ultracold atomic, and photonic systems, where synthetic non-Abelian gauge fields enable phenomena such as spin transport, the spin-Hall effect, and polarization control. These systems provide access to gauge-field dynamics beyond the reach of high-energy experiments. In all the above mentioned cases, the state of the system evolves in an effective external YM field. Here, we report the results of a classical study (as preparatory for a full quantum study) of particle dynamics in constant gauge fields produced by constant gauge potentials, by focusing on configurations that are experimentally relevant. We show that consequences such as unbounded trajectories in a constant color magnetic field and unusual correlation between charge and color dynamics have a direct bearing on the physical phenomena observed, especially in experiments involving charge and spin transports. More generally, this work also shows how the low energy systems can act as laboratories to probe quintessentially non-Abelian features such as the Wu-Yang ambiguity.

title: Observing quantum-classical correspondence through optical path integrals
authors: Li-Man Tian, Yunfei Wang, Ying Zhou, Chang Li, Shanchao Zhang, Xuan Dai, Bai-Chuan Long, Hui Yan, Shi-Liang Zhu and Yong-Li Wen
abstract: The quantum–classical correspondence (QCC) describes how quantum systems recover classical behavior in the semiclassical limit. One of the crucial mechanisms to this correspondence is the concept of action, which governs dynamics in both classical mechanics and quantum path integrals. Despite its fundamental importance, experimental access to the action of individual quantum paths remains crucial yet challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a method to measure the action of quantum paths between fixed spacetime points, based on weak-value measurement techniques. By introducing and analyzing the spectrum of the norm of the action gradient, we identify not only single but also multiple stationary-action paths in systems exhibiting complex QCC. Using an optical setup that simulates photon propagation in free space and under an impulsive potential, we reconstruct pathwise actions and observe sharp dips in the spectrum that correspond precisely to classical trajectories. This work provides a framework for directly accessing and analyzing the action, opening new avenues for experimentally exploring the QCC.

title: Algebraic structures of the Lindblad equation
authors: Leonel Bixano, Guillermo López-Alvarez, Victor Alberto Cruz-Barriguete, Víctor Guadalupe Ibarra-Sierra, José Luis Cardoso, Juan Carlos Sandoval-Santana and Alejandro Kunold
abstract: We investigate the algebraic structure underlying the Lindblad equation for finite-dimensional open quantum systems. Using an orthonormal Hermitian operator basis, we represent the Liouville superoperator in a model-independent basis of Hermitian superoperators realizing the standard left–right multiplication maps. We express their multiplication, commutator, and anticommutator relations explicitly in terms of the Lie and Jordan structure constants of the underlying operator basis. This formulation makes explicit how dissipative contributions can extend the generator beyond the adjoint Lie algebra associated with purely Hamiltonian evolution. The multiplication rules allow us to derive differential equations for the expansion coefficients of the dynamical map. We further derive recursion relations for the iterative construction of the algebra in multiqubit systems. For a fixed operator basis, the algebraic data can be precomputed and reused, while the Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters enter through a single set of coefficients. Computational benchmarks compare memory usage and construction time for algebraic, direct, and standard Kronecker implementations. For the cases tested, the algebraic implementation reduces peak memory requirements and construction time relative to the direct implementation. In the benchmarks, the standard Kronecker implementation requires less memory and time than both alternatives and enables calculations for larger numbers of qubits. These findings establish the computational limitations of the present algebraic implementation alongside its explicit characterization of the underlying superoperator algebra. An accompanying Mathematica notebook provides five examples covering algebraic verification for one-, two-, and three-qubit operator bases and numerical transmon dynamics. The examples confirm agreement with the direct method, illustrate an approximate gate and population leakage beyond the computational subspace, and use Choi matrices to check Hermiticity preservation, complete positivity, and trace preservation.

title: Quantum algorithm for evaluating Lyapunov stability of non-Hermitian systems
abstract: Stability is a fundamental property of dynamical systems, and Lyapunov theory provides a rigorous link between stability and eigenvalue distribution. By computing eigenvalues, quantum algorithms may offer potential advantages for evaluating the stability of high-dimensional systems under appropriate assumptions regarding data access and quantum resource requirements. In this work, we introduce a quantum algorithm based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) to efficiently resolve the complex eigenspectrum of non-Hermitian matrices and determine asymptotic stability. By employing block encoding and QSVT techniques, we implement a polynomial transformation to approximate the singular value threshold problem, enabling the localization of eigenvalues with positive real parts under appropriate requirements regarding block encoding efficiency, matrix conditioning, state overlap, and precision. We validate the method numerically on a one-dimensional non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain with local gain and loss, demonstrating accurate detection of unstable and stable cases, which is consistent with the results obtained by exact diagonalization. These results show that our quantum algorithm is a reliable and powerful tool for stability analysis and spectral characterization of high-dimensional dynamical systems.
